sample_unit: contrast-enhanced CT scans (training); external validation n=54 GBC, 81 public lymph node, 606 multicancer
models_evaluated: ConLymphNet (3D nnUNet with vertebral landmark region selection)

links.outcome: Radiologist detection and segmentation performance with versus without AI assistance
links.effect: AI assistance improved radiologists' performance significantly, particularly for less experienced readers (detection rate +20.2%, segmentation accuracy +13.0%, P < .001), while reducing false positives by 33.3%.
links.quote: AI assistance improved radiologists' performance significantly, particularly for less experienced readers (detection rate +20.2%, segmentation accuracy +13.0%, P < .001), while reducing false positives by 33.3%.

links.outcome: AI model detection rate and processing time compared with radiologists
links.effect: Model detection rate 89.6% comparable with experienced residents (89.2%); processing time 28.7 ± 12.4 s vs 165.3 ± 47.8 s.
links.quote: The model's detection rate (89.6%) was comparable with experienced residents (89.2%) but with reduced processing time (28.7 ± 12.4s v 165.3 ± 47.8 s).

links.outcome: Segmentation Dice performance across internal and external sites
links.effect: Mean Dice 0.696 ± 0.179 internal cross-validation, 0.631 ± 0.187 external GBC, 0.639 ± 0.176 public lymph node data sets; modest drop externally.
links.quote: ConLymphNet achieved mean Dice coefficients of 0.696 ± 0.179, 0.631 ± 0.187, and 0.639 ± 0.176 and low false-positive rates of 0.78 ± 0.35, 0.81 ± 0.33, 0.93 ± 0.47/volume on internal cross-validation, external GBC, and public lymph node data sets, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Anatomic landmark-based region constraint preprocessing to improve segmentation
Public release of expert-verified lymph node segmentations for reproducibility

screen.reason: The study tests the incremental value and clinical impact of AI assistance on radiologist reading and segmentation performance across experience levels in a reader study.
